title: kbmon names an orphan process only after a minute and says when it has a live child, never that nothing waits for it
goal: kbmon's sessions headline and needs-you line name an orphan process (class orphan) only once it is at least 60 s old; an orphan's line in both says `with a live child` when one of its children still runs; the sessions headline drops the claim `nothing waits for them`

run:
import atexit,shutil,tempfile
_m=tempfile.mkdtemp
def _d(*a,**k):
 d=_m(*a,**k);atexit.register(shutil.rmtree,d,True);return d
tempfile.mkdtemp=_d
import os, re, sys, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path
home = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA"] = home
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"] = os.getcwd()
os.environ["KB_COORD_STORE"] = home + "/none.db"
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import bl_procs, mon_base, mon_needs, mon_sessions, mon_status
here = str(Path('.').resolve())
t = int(time.time())
tab = {90003: (1, t - 5, "sh"), 90007: (1, t - 120, "sh"), 90008: (90007, t - 120, "sleep"), 90009: (1, t - 300, "sh")}
bl_procs.process_table = lambda: dict(tab)
bl_procs.cwd_map = lambda: ({p: here for p in tab}, None)
bl_procs.leads_group = lambda pid: False
data = mon_sessions.collect(mon_base.Ctx(root=Path(here)))
snap = {"taken": "2026-11-08T12:00:00Z", "panels": {"sessions": {"state": "ok", "data": data}}}
text = "\n".join(mon_status.answer(snap, "sessions")["lines"])
needs = mon_needs.line(snap)
print(text, needs, sep="\n")
bad = ("nothing waits for them" in text or "pid 90003" in text or "pid 90003" in needs or not text.startswith("Sessions: 2 orphan processes")
       or not re.search(r"pid 90007\b[^\n]*with a live child", text) or not re.search(r"orphan pid 90007\b[^;]*with a live child", needs)
       or re.search(r"pid 90009\b[^\n]*live child", text) or re.search(r"orphan pid 90009\b[^;]*live child", needs)
       or "pid 90009" not in text or "pid 90009" not in needs)
sys.exit(not not bad)

gates.question: How does kbmon decide an orphan has a live child, and does the sessions.orphan alert take the 60 s rule?
options: child from listed processes, alert unchanged
child from listed processes, alert takes the 60 s rule
gates.recommendation: child from listed processes, alert unchanged
gates.reason: the goal names the headline and needs-you line only; a child is any listed process whose parent is the orphan, so a child with a working directory outside the clone is not seen
gates.answer: child from listed processes, alert unchanged

notes: Evidence 2026-11-08: orphan sh loops around sleep (pids 46638 and 88109 that day) have a live child, and the code cannot know that nothing waits for an orphan (mon_status prints the claim today and listed 'orphan pid 86144, running 1s'). The earlier live check (the claim absent from the live sessions answer) is replaced: it passes whenever no orphan runs.
